head_to_head.text:
**Sprint Retrospective — Narrative Summary**

The retrospective focused on a candid accounting of what went wrong in the last sprint, with the discussion converging on three operational issues and one human one: unclear requirements, a late-discovered dependency, communication gaps between two subteams, and growing concern about team morale.

Unclear requirements emerged as the most persistent frustration. The team described entering the sprint without a shared, concrete understanding of the work, which led to diverging interpretations, rework, and effort spent on the wrong things. Several people noted that the ambiguity wasn't surfaced until well into the sprint, by which point correcting course was costly.

Closely related was the dependency that came to light too late. Because it wasn't identified during planning, it disrupted work already in progress and forced last-minute re-prioritization. The discussion suggested this problem and the requirements problem reinforced each other: when the scope and shape of the work aren't clear, cross-workstream dependencies are easy to miss until they become blockers.

Communication gaps between the two subteams drew significant attention as well. Work proceeded in parallel without adequate coordination, producing mismatched assumptions and friction at handoff points. The absence of regular shared touchpoints and clear ownership of integration points came up as likely contributing factors.

Finally, several people raised morale directly. The combination of churn, rework, and firefighting has taken a visible toll, and there was concern that if the underlying issues go unaddressed, frustration and disengagement will deepen. Importantly, morale wasn't framed as a separate problem but as a downstream effect of the sprint's operational failures — a signal that the other themes carry real human cost.

Taken together, the discussion pointed to a sprint that struggled less because of individual effort than because of structural gaps: how requirements get clarified, how dependencies get discovered, and how the subteams stay connected.
